subject: Post-call: SLO measurement protocols, prompt governance & harness artifacts
messages:
From: Taylor Brooks <taylor@acme.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME SRE Team <sre@acme.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up on SLO targets & measurement approach

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call earlier — that was helpful. Quick recap / asks from our side so we can scope the qualification run: 

- Latency targets: 95th percentile under 220ms for single-turn completions (avg token length ~45). We also want p99 under 400ms for critical checkout flows.
- Concurrency: baseline load will be 60 concurrent streams, peak 160, with warm caches for 70% of requests.
- Streaming: we need chunked token streaming with resume support and client-side ordering guarantees (we can mock on our playground).
- Throughput: bursts up to 750 tokens/sec sustained for 2 minutes on smaller prompt bundles.

To proceed we need your measurement definition (how you compute p95/p99 at token vs generation completion), the prompt set you’ll use, and a short repro recipe so our SREs can run a dry replay. Can you share a minimal harness config and the prompt bundle you intend to use?

Also, can you confirm whether you will run the controlled qualification in your dedicated infra or in our VPC? We prefer VPC for the data path.

Thanks — attaching our sample traffic characteristics in case it helps.

—Taylor
Taylor Brooks
Head of AI Ops, ACME Retail
T: +1 415 555 0119

Attachment: acme_traffic_profile_v1.csv (stub)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Brooks <taylor@acme.ai>
Cc: ACME SRE Team <sre@acme.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on SLO targets & measurement approach

Hi Taylor — great to connect. Short answers up front, and a proposed lightweight plan below.

- Measurement defs: we compute latency at two points (1) token-latency: time from request arrival to first-token emitted; (2) completion-latency: time to final token for the primary response. P95/P99 are computed over completion-latency unless the prompt indicates streaming-critical semantics — in which case we report time-to-first-byte and time-to-nth-byte (configurable). We include sampling windows and warm-cache flags in the reported CSV.

- Prompt set: attached is a sanitized prompt bank (acme_prompt_bank_v1.jsonl) that mirrors the flows you described. It includes metadata tags (flow:checkout|recommendation, stream_required:true/false, expected_tokens: est).

- Repro recipe & harness: attached repro_instructions_v1.md plus a short measurement protocol (redwood_measurement_protocol_v0.3.pdf). The protocol includes: request sequencing, concurrency shaping, KV-cache warmup policy, and aggregation buckets (per-route, per-model, per-run).

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
1) You confirm VPC vs Redwood-hosted: if VPC we’ll share an infra checklist; if hosted we’ll provision a temporary dedicated pool. (Reply by 2027-10-06)
2) ACME SRE to run dry replay of our prompt set with their traffic profile; we’ll run a mirrored run on our side for parity. (Target window 2027-10-08 — 2027-10-09)
3) Joint readout with L3 perf traces and token-level latency breakdown (2027-10-11)

Ben and Rishi — can you review the attached harness snippets and confirm whether the default KV-warmup policy (70%) and streaming chunk size (256B) look correct for their expected flows?

I’ll follow-up with a calendar invite once Taylor confirms environment.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_prompt_bank_v1.jsonl (stub), redwood_measurement_protocol_v0.3.pdf (stub), repro_instructions_v1.md (stub)
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up on SLO targets & measurement approach

Kim / Rishi — forwarding Taylor’s note and Kimberley’s attachments. Quick notes from me after a skim: 

- KV warmup: 70% seems reasonable as a starting point; we should capture both cold-start and warm-start windows explicitly. I’ll add a run that flips warm-cache to 30% to see sensitivity.
- Streaming chunking: 256B is fine; suggest we also emit a trace marker at first-chunk and nth-chunk for per-chunk latency histograms.
- Measurement aggregation: include both request-level and token-level histograms; p95 completion-latency may mask degenerate token-drop events — add an anomaly detector that flags high variance runs.

Action items:
- Rishi: can you prepare two harness configs (warm70.json and warm30.json) and upload to the shared Drive by EOD 2027-10-05?
- I’ll draft the run orchestration script and the perf-trace collection patch (will reference redwood_measurement_protocol_v0.3.pdf).

Thanks — will coordinate once Taylor confirms environment preference.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Perf & Measurement, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-10-06T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on SLO targets & measurement approach

Kim / Ben / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. ACME prefers the VPC run (we want control of ingress/egress). We’ve scoped resources and SRE can run the dry replay on 2027-10-08 morning (US-PST).

A couple of clarifications before the run: 
- Please include the token-level time-to-first-chunk and time-to-completion metrics.
- For p99 reporting, include a short appendix showing the top 10 request hashes that drove the tail so we can correlate to application flows.
- We will also validate resume-on-failure for streaming; can you surface the resume token semantics in the repro doc?

If you can share the Drive folder with the harness configs and a short checklist for the VPC sandbox by EOD 2027-10-06, we’ll schedule the run and loop in infra.

Confirmed: 2027-10-08 09:30 PT for dry replay. Please send an invite and the Drive link.

—Taylor
Taylor Brooks
Head of AI Ops, ACME Retail
